$comment: Ninth family. Authored at step F of the certification method, AFTER the falsification
attacks rather than before them, so that two defects already found end to end appear here as
requirements rather than as loose bugs:
SECURITY_POSITION_SETTLED       is_secured is now a declared answer. It was inferred from
whether a free-text box held a 'meaningful value', so a
borrower writing 'None — this is an unsecured loan' got a
secured loan and a security clause describing collateral
that did not exist.
ENFORCEMENT_MATCHES_THE_LOAN    LOAN_SARFAESI_ENFORCEMENT_001 declares itself invalid where
the loan is unsecured, in its own invalid_if, and the
blueprint gates it on lender eligibility alone. The
knowledge base is more correct than the gate.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. No requirement asserts that a given interest rate is usurious,
that a limitation period has run, or that a charge is void for non-registration. Those are
legal conclusions. What is authored is what the instrument must ADDRESS, and the assessment
reports whether it does.
Two clauses in this family carry invalid_if conditions that no requirement can currently
evaluate -- 'Mortgage not registered with Sub-Registrar', 'Charge not registered with ROC
within 30 days'. They are FORMALITY requirements below, capped at PROVIDED_FOR, because the
document can provide for an act and cannot perform it.

requirements.statement: The sum advanced, and how it reaches the borrower, are stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and there is no ascertainable sum to repay: the instrument records an intention to lend and nothing a court could order repaid.

requirements.statement: The borrower's obligation to repay, and the times at which repayment falls due, are stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and an advance with no stated obligation to return it is not a loan at all — the instrument describes a transfer and leaves the parties to argue about what it was.
$timing_note: NOT authored as a TIMING requirement. Whether a limitation period has begun, and from
what, turns on whether the loan is repayable on demand or on a date — and the system
holds no field distinguishing them. Reporting a computed window here would be the
cheque-notice proxy defect in a new place: an answer computed from a stand-in for the

requirements.statement: Whether interest runs on the advance, and on what basis, is settled by the instrument.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and neither party can compute what is owed on any given day, and the sum demanded on default rests on nothing the agreement says.

requirements.statement: The events that constitute default are identified.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and every remedy in the instrument has no trigger: the lender may act on a default the agreement never defines.

requirements.statement: What the lender may do on default is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and default is named and nothing follows from it.

requirements.statement: Where the loan is secured, what secures it is identified in the instrument.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a secured loan names no security, so there is nothing for the default and enforcement provisions to attach to and nothing the borrower has agreed to create.
$position_note: is_secured is a DECLARED answer (loan_is_secured: Yes/No), not an inference from the
collateral description. Unanswered leaves this APPLICABILITY_UNKNOWN, which is the
honest state: nobody has said whether this loan is secured.

requirements.statement: An unsecured loan does not assert enforcement remedies that exist only over security.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and an unsecured loan can carry a clause entitling the lender to take possession of, manage and transfer 'the secured assets' without the intervention of any court — over assets that do not exist.
requirements.coherence_note: LOAN_SARFAESI_ENFORCEMENT_001 lists 'Loan is unsecured' in its own invalid_if, and the blueprint gates it on lender eligibility alone.
$split: One of the two branches the guarded clause declares. Authored alone it left the other uncovered.

requirements.statement: A lender that cannot invoke the enforcement statute does not assert rights under it.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a loan from a lender outside the class the Act confers these rights on can still carry a clause acknowledging the lender as a secured creditor entitled to enforce without a court.
requirements.coherence_note: LOAN_SARFAESI_ENFORCEMENT_001 lists 'Lender is not a SARFAESI-eligible secured creditor' in its own invalid_if, and the clause's closing sentence says it 'shall not be construed to confer SARFAESI rights on a lender not so eligible'.
$split: The branch the original requirement omitted. A secured loan from an ineligible lender
ships the clause and was outside any requirement.
VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE: lender_is_regulated is derived from lender_type and is NOT the
same question as whether a lender is a 'secured creditor' within the meaning of the Act.
The clause's own text names 'a scheduled bank or notified financial institution / NBFC'.
Whether the derived flag tracks that class is a legal question and the flag is being used
here as the closest established fact, not as an answer to it.
requirements.$verification_needed: SARFAESI Act, 2002 s.2(1)(zd) — which lenders are 'secured creditors' able to invoke the Act, and whether lender_type distinguishes them.

requirements.statement: Where the loan is secured, the instrument provides for the registrations that perfect the security.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the agreement creates security and says nothing about the steps that make it effective against third parties, leaving a lender who believes itself secured with an interest nobody else is bound to notice.
requirements.outside_the_document: Registration of a mortgage with the Sub-Registrar and of a charge with the Registrar of Companies are acts performed after execution. The clause can require them; it cannot accomplish them, and a positive finding here says only that the instrument provides for them.

requirements.statement: Whether the borrower may repay early, and on what terms, is settled.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a borrower with the money cannot know whether tendering it discharges the debt or breaches the agreement.

falsification.attack: Wrote the collateral description as a plain-English negative — 'None — this is an unsecured loan', which is what the field's own help text instructed — then generated the agreement from a scheduled-bank lender.
falsification.false_green: is_secured was inferred from whether the free-text box held a 'meaningful value', so the explicit negative became an affirmative position: a security clause describing collateral that does not exist, and a SARFAESI clause asserting the lender could take possession of the secured assets without a court. After the position was made a declared Yes/No, the security clause was STILL re-injected by dependencyResolver through LOAN_DEFAULT_001.required_with, and SARFAESI still shipped because its gate reads lender eligibility alone.
